evals.name: extract-first-rule
evals.prompt: I want to redesign the Header component in my React app. The Header.tsx file already exists in src/components/Header.tsx. Should I rebuild it from scratch in the mockup sandbox, or is there a better approach?

expectations.text: Response states the golden rule: if the component exists in the codebase, extract it — never rebuild from memory.
Response warns that rebuilding from scratch produces wrong values: specifically dimensions, colours, spacing, opacity values, and font sizes.
Response mentions creating Current.tsx in the group folder as the extracted baseline, imported alongside _group.css with the app's :root CSS variables.
Response directs the user to read the mockup-extract skill for the full extraction process (import chain tracing, dependency classification as inline/copy/stub).

evals.name: design-subagent-brief-anatomy
evals.prompt: I'm generating two variant designs of my dashboard card in the mockup sandbox using DESIGN subagents. What must my subagent brief include, and what must I leave out?

expectations.text: Response lists the required DESIGN subagent brief anatomy fields: Product/brand identity, Goal, Vibe, Target location, and Variant hypothesis.
Response explicitly states NOT to include specific CSS values, colours, font names, pixel spacing, layout prescriptions, section names, or design style names.
Response says each subagent must get a distinct brief — a different variant hypothesis — so they produce genuinely distinct output rather than three nearly identical variants.
Response describes the variant labelling convention: label by design hypothesis not letter alone — e.g. 'A — Minimal' / 'B — Editorial' / 'C — Bold' — so the user can say 'I prefer B' precisely.

evals.name: graduation-gate-and-subagent-choice
evals.prompt: The user approved variant B of my redesigned checkout form mockup. Before I graduate it to the main app, what questions must I answer, and which type of subagent handles graduation?

expectations.text: Response specifies a GENERAL subagent (not a DESIGN subagent) for graduation — explicitly stating DESIGN subagents do not wire APIs or understand routing.
Response lists the three graduation decision gate questions: which variant exactly, whether the main app's component library differs from shadcn/ui, and whether the mockup has real or mock data.

Response states to graduate exactly what was approved — do not improve the design during graduation — preserving colours, gradients, shadows, border radius, spacing, typography, layout structure, animations, hover states, and icons.
Response describes what to transform during graduation: mock data → real API calls, no-op navigation handlers → real router links, local constants → app state, stubbed auth → real auth context.
